items.t: Cruise control switch can start an engine fire (recall)

items.note: Free disconnect service under Ford recall 05S28 (NHTSA 05V388). The recall page cited is for the twin 1996 F-150; check the Bronco VIN with a Ford dealer.

items.t: Tailgate rear window can shatter on its own
items.job: Replace heated tailgate glass and tailgate glass run channel seal
items.note: Glass prices are new aftermarket heated drop-down back glass for 1988-1996 Bronco ($163-$199) plus the LMR tailgate-side run channel seal ($20). No source states a book time; one owner reported a glass shop quote of $230 installed, so the labor range is kept short.

items.t: Anti-lock brakes fail or pull to one side
items.job: Replace a failed ABS wheel speed sensor (after an ABS code and brake check)
items.note: Priced for the most common fix, a wheel speed sensor (1A Auto: $25-$57 for 1996 Bronco sensors). YourMechanic lists a 1994 Bronco rear sensor job at $234 ($265-$322 at shops). If the shop finds a sticking caliper, leaking line or a bad ABS hydraulic unit instead, the cost will be different.

items.t: E4OD automatic transmission slipping or failing
items.job: Replace with a remanufactured E4OD transmission
items.note: Remanufactured 4WD E4OD units for 1995-1996 Bronco list at $2,595 (SP Precision) to $3,625 (Powertrain Company), plus a refundable core charge; one owner reported about $2,400 for a rebuilt unit and about $700 labor to install it. Hours are based on that owner-reported labor, as no book time was found. Minor faults (solenoids, fluid) can cost far less, so get a diagnosis first.
